one_month_reasoning: Revised. Q3 2026 results are now more likely inside the window than not (about 65%). Hudbay's 2026 6-K filing dates run about two weeks ahead of 2025 (Q1 on 1 May vs 13 May; Q2 on 29 Jul vs 13 Aug; EDGAR index). Aggregators list Oct 28, not yet company-confirmed, and call notices usually come about three weeks ahead. The bar is high: consensus is $0.36-0.37 against a Q2 actual of $0.28. Copper was flat to up in Q3, but gold is lower than its Q2 average. H1 copper output was 56.2kt, running at the low end of the 110-138kt guide, so a Q3 print that implies a guidance trim is the main downside risk. Past HBM post-earnings moves have been large in both directions. The Snow Lake mine-life upgrade (Sep 28) is fresh. The supervisor points to an Oct-2 intraday print of about $27.20 on thin volume, and I give it only a small weight. 2026-10-31 is a Saturday, so the effective mark is the Oct 30 close. Other in-window events are the Oct 28 FOMC and China's October data, which reach HBM via copper. I used a lognormal with a median of $26.30 (about +0.5%, from the Snow Lake news and a small early-October drift) and a monthly sigma of 19%: base 18% (0.63/3.5) widened for the probable earnings event.

fair_value.method: Blend of four methods. EV/EBITDA: 2027E EBITDA $1.50B x 7.0x less ~$20M attributable net debt / 444.1M = $23.6. SOTP: operations 6x $1.5B plus Copper World 70% at $1.2B, Cactus at $0.8B and other at $0.2B = $25.2. P/E: $1.65 2027E x 14.5x = $23.9. FCF yield: $500M / 4.5% = $25.0. Weights 30/30/25/15 give about $24.4, up from $23.5 after building in guided 2027 volume growth, current consensus and the reported share count. It stays below spot and below the supervisor's $27 because I value on a mid-cycle-leaning metals deck rather than near-record spot.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E adj. EBITDA $1.50B x 7.0x = $10.5B EV; less ~$0.02B attributable net debt; / 444.1M shares

inputs_detail.value: 56.2kt (low end of the 2026 guide on an annualized basis)

inputs_detail.derivation: I start from LTM $1.27B (on about 115kt Cu) and add about $0.23B for +35kt of copper to ~150kt, which is below the 162kt guidance midpoint because H1-26 ran at the low end of guidance, at about $6.7k/t incremental margin on a $5.5/lb deck. I add about $0.10B because the deck is above the LTM realized copper price. I subtract about $0.12B for gold falling to about $3,800/oz from about $4,300 realized on flat 213-269koz guidance. Net about $1.48-1.50B. That is below the supervisor's $1.55-1.7B because my deck sits between Cochilco's $5.10 and BofA's $6.12 2027 copper calls rather than near spot.

Was 7.5x on NTM/LTM-like EBITDA. Now applied to a higher, growth-inclusive 2027 EBITDA, so I trim it to 7.0x. Mid-tier copper producers have traded at about 5-8x mid-cycle and de-rate after copper peaks (2011 and 2015 analogs).

inputs_detail.value: ~$20M (reported net cash $80.5M less 30% of the $334.5M Copper World LLC cash attributable to Mitsubishi)
inputs_detail.derivation: -80.5 + 0.3 x 334.5 = about +20. This matches the supervisor's reconciliation of the Q2 MD&A net-debt footnote.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Producing ops $1.5B x 6.0x = $9.0B; Copper World 70% $1.2B; Cactus $0.8B; Mason/other $0.2B; less $0.02B net debt = $11.18B / 444.1M

inputs_detail.derivation: I use the low-to-middle of the 5-8x mid-cycle range because growth assets are valued separately here.

Mitsubishi paid $600M for 30%, which implies about $1.4B for Hudbay's 70%. The PFS NPV8 is $1.1B at $3.75/lb, with +$0.6B per +$0.50/lb. Capex is expected above the 2023 PFS, the DFS and sanction are still pending (late 2026), and there is permitting litigation, so I apply a roughly 15% haircut to the Mitsubishi mark.
Hudbay issued shares worth $1,135.6M (note 4). I haircut that by about 30% because the asset is pre-development (PFS due 2027) and the price was paid at near-record copper.
A nominal option value for Mason (Nevada) and exploration, since the PFS is not yet complete.

Current consensus annualizes to about $1.45 on 444M shares at roughly spot metals. I add guided copper volume growth of about +25% and assume a 10-15% lower copper and gold deck. Net about +14%, giving about $1.65. This replaces the stale July-2025 Stifel $0.27/qtr input, which the supervisor discounted.
Trailing P/E is about 13.7x at near-record metals. 14.5x on forward earnings credits growth, but it is below the 15x I used in round 1 because the EPS base now already includes the volume step-up.

H1 annualizes to about $400M. 2027 volume growth adds about $0.15-0.2B after tax. Copper World and New Ingerbelle growth capex take back part of that, though Copper World is part-funded by Mitsubishi and the $334.5M ring-fenced cash.
Raised from 4.0% because FCF is now measured on a growth-inclusive, higher-volume base near a cyclical high in metals.

bear.story: Copper mean-reverts toward Cochilco's $5.10 or below (sub-$4.75/lb) and gold corrects. Copper Mountain's ramp misses, so 2027 copper lands near the 140kt low end, and Copper World sanction brings capex inflation or a funding draw on the F-10 shelf. EBITDA falls toward $0.9-1.0B and miners de-rate as in 2011, 2015 and 2022 (copper equities -35-55%).

base.story: Copper eases to $5.5-6.0/lb and gold stays firm. 2027 delivers about 150kt of copper and $1.4-1.6B of EBITDA, Copper World is sanctioned with Mitsubishi funding, and the stock holds about 7x forward EBITDA. This fits the base rate: a median of about 1.05x in the year after a >50% annual gain.

bull.story: Copper holds at $6.5/lb or more (BofA's record 2027 call or above) and the guided 160kt-plus volume arrives. EBITDA reaches $1.9B or more and the Copper World DFS and sanction re-rate NAV. The stock breaks the $32 high, in line with HBM's +65-90% follow-through years.

thesis_break_reason: About -39%. At $16 the market cap (~$7.1B) is under 5x my $1.5B 2027E EBITDA, with nothing for Copper World (Mitsubishi-implied about $1.4B for 70%) or Cactus (about $1.1B paid in stock). A trade there would most likely mean copper sustained below about $4.75/lb, a failed Copper Mountain ramp against the 140-184kt guide, a Copper World capex or funding shock forcing equity issuance, or a Constancia/Peru disruption, not ordinary 55-60%-vol noise. It sits just above the late-2025 breakout zone (52-week low $14.34). I raised it from $15.5 because the reported share count and volume guidance raise the fundamental floor.

key_uncertainties: Copper price path: spot is about $6.5/lb vs. Cochilco's 2027 forecast of $5.10 and BofA's $6.12. HBM equity carries about 1.5-2x copper beta.
Execution on the 2027 volume step-up: H1-26 copper of 56.2kt ran at the low end of the 2026 guide, and Copper Mountain must nearly double output.
Gold by-product credits (38% of Q2 revenue) and a flat gold guide (213-269koz in 2027).

reasoning: Round-2 revision. The base-rate anchor is unchanged: 137 overlapping 12-month HBM log returns since 2014 have a median of about 1.09x and an IQR of 0.71-1.64x. After >50% trailing gains the median is about 1.05x, with a range of 0.52x-1.9x. Realized annualized vol is about 62% over the full history and 54% over the last 24 months. I accepted the supervisor's fact corrections and verified the key ones in primary filings. (1) 2027 copper guidance is 140-184kt vs 110-138kt in 2026 (March 2026 6-K). My round-1 NTM EBITDA of $1.30B ignored this, so I rebuilt 2027E EBITDA at $1.50B. (2) Shares are 444.1M (reported). (3) The stale Stifel $0.27/qtr was replaced by the current $0.36-0.37 Q3 consensus. (4) EDGAR filing dates confirm 2026 reporting runs about two weeks earlier than 2025, so Q3 is probably in the 1-month window. (5) The Mitsubishi $180M is due by about July 2027. (6) Oct-1 closed at $26.18, and the $27.20 was an Oct-2 intraday print. I also used the attributable net-debt treatment (about $20M) and added a SOTP leg with Cactus re-based to the $1,135.6M actually paid. Fair value rises from $23.5 to $24.4. I part ways with the supervisor's $27 on two points. First, I value on a metals deck between Cochilco and BofA rather than near spot, because copper is near record highs and mining multiples compress after peaks (2011 and 2015). Second, H1-26 output ran at the low end of guidance, so I haircut 2027 volume to about 150kt. For the distribution, the guided volume growth and the base-rate median after strong years (1.05x, about $27.5) pull the centre up, and fair value below spot pulls it down. I set the 12-month median at $25.8, up from $25, with a lognormal sigma of 0.55 and a slightly fattened far-left tail for copper-rout analogs. That gives P(>=26) of 0.49 (was 0.47). The 15.5/25.5/39 scenario mixture at 25/50/25 is consistent with this. Research was limited this round: AAII was blocked by bot protection, so the $0.37 consensus figure rests on the supervisor's citation plus Earnings Whispers. No option prices or implied volatility were consulted.
